policy: Exact commits resolved with 'git ls-remote' and shallow clones on 2026-09-27. Inference has NOT been run for any backend yet: the reconnaissance sandbox had no GPU and its network policy blocked huggingface.co, ml-site.cdn-apple.com and download.pytorch.org. 'gpu_smoke_test' records that honestly.

repositories.name: splatline
repositories.model_license: n/a (wraps SHARP, TripoSplat, VGGT, DepthSplat, LongSplat)
repositories.windows: not targeted (macOS-first, Electron player needs Node)
repositories.integration: Architecture reference only: pluggable --splat-backend design and per-backend license table informed our Backend contract. No code copied.
repositories.findings: README lists TripoSplat (MIT) as a commercial-safe single-image 3DGS option — candidate for a future photo backend.

repositories.name: recon3d
repositories.windows: plausible: pure-Python + torch; depends on gsplat (prebuilt Windows wheels only for some torch/CUDA combos), gtsam and open3d wheels
repositories.vram: README: 'works on 8GB GPUs' via chunking; VGGT ~40 frames/batch on 24 GB; we use chunk 20 on 16 GB
repositories.install: pip install recon3d[all] + vggt + MoGe from source (we install from GitHub commit archives with --no-deps)
repositories.outputs: scene.ply, scene.splat, scene.obj (TSDF), transforms.json (OpenGL c2w), COLMAP sparse

repositories.name: vggt
repositories.code_license: VGGT License v1 (2025-07-29, commercial use permitted except military)
repositories.model_license: facebook/VGGT-1B: non-commercial; facebook/VGGT-1B-Commercial: commercial, gated (application form)
repositories.vram: 1B params; ~40 frames per batch on 24 GB (recon3d README)

repositories.name: moge
repositories.model_license: UNVERIFIED — HF model cards unreachable from the sandbox; treated as non-commercial until verified
repositories.windows: plausible: v2 inference path needs torch, utils3d_moge, pipeline (pure Python); flex_gemm is only needed for v3 sparse modules
repositories.vram: ViT-S/ViT-L single image well under 8 GB (to be measured)
repositories.integration: backend 'moge_rgbd' via workers/moge_worker.py in runtime 'photo-cu128' (experimental); newly added to the matrix during reconnaissance

repositories.name: one2scene
repositories.code_license: NONE (no LICENSE file: all rights reserved by default)
repositories.windows: no (Linux CUDA scripts, several source installs)
repositories.vram: denoise checkpoint alone ~19 GB on disk; exceeds a comfortable 16 GB VRAM budget without offload work

repositories.name: sharp
repositories.model_license: Apple Machine Learning Research Model License — research purposes only, non-commercial (LICENSE_MODEL)
repositories.windows: plausible: pure PyTorch prediction (CPU/CUDA/MPS); gsplat only for its own video rendering
repositories.vram: to be measured; Splatline reports ~2.5 GB checkpoint
repositories.entry_point: sharp predict -i DIR -o DIR -c sharp_2572gikvuh.pt -> <stem>.ply (OpenCV convention, sRGB SH DC)
repositories.integration: backend 'sharp' (research profile only; user downloads weights after accepting the Apple license)

repositories.name: longsplat
repositories.code_license: NVIDIA Source Code License (non-commercial) + Inria Gaussian-Splatting License
repositories.windows: requires compiling simple-knn, diff-gaussian-rasterization, fused-ssim, optional RoPE kernels (MSVC + CUDA toolkit)

repositories.name: depthsplat
repositories.model_license: haofeixu/depthsplat on HF (to verify); uses Depth-Anything-V2 (Small Apache-2.0, Base/Large CC-BY-NC-4.0)
repositories.windows: unknown (PyTorch 2.4 / CUDA 12.4; dataset-oriented CLI via hydra)
repositories.vram: training on 4x RTX 4090 documented; inference not measured
repositories.note: The URL in the original plan (DongLiangSXU/DepthSplat) does not resolve; the official repository is cvg/depthsplat.

repositories.name: gsfixer
repositories.windows: no (tested CUDA 12.1 on H20/H100; compiled rasteriser extensions)

repositories.name: gsfix3d
repositories.code_license: Apache-2.0 + Inria Gaussian-Splatting License (non-commercial for the whole project)
repositories.vram: tested on RTX 4500 Ada (24 GB); per-scene diffusion fine-tuning

repositories.name: gsplat
repositories.windows: prebuilt wheels for some torch/CUDA combos at https://docs.gsplat.studio/whl; otherwise JIT compile (needs MSVC + CUDA toolkit)
repositories.integration: inside runtimes (SHARP dependency, recon3d training). The application's own preview/VR180 renderer is a numpy reference renderer.

repositories.name: depth-anything-v2
repositories.windows: yes (pure PyTorch; also ONNX exports exist)
repositories.integration: candidate commercial-safe fallback (relative depth only, needs FOV assumption); newly added

repositories.model_license: Apple license (same LICENSE file) — verify commercial terms
